summary:
TwinWorld is an interactive, data-driven platform developed to identify and rank Earth locations that may serve as environmental analogs for selected Moon and Mars exploration targets. It addresses the challenge by comparing terrestrial locations using four measurable criteria: terrain slope, temperature, rainfall, and vegetation.

Users can select a planetary target, explore ranked Earth locations, customize criteria weights, and visualize how different environmental conditions affect similarity scores. The platform includes a 3D globe, downloadable results, a validation section comparing model rankings with documented analogs, and a methodology section explaining the data, assumptions, and limitations.

Using NASA datasets, Google Earth Engine, Python, and web technologies, TwinWorld provides a transparent and accessible tool to support planetary exploration research and education. Rather than claiming to identify exact twins, it offers a systematic starting point for discovering potential Earth analogs and understanding where further research is needed.
details:
TwinWorld is an interactive web-based platform designed to explore terrestrial analogs for Moon and Mars missions. It uses environmental and terrain data to compare locations on Earth with selected planetary targets.

The platform evaluates locations using four main indicators: terrain slope, temperature, rainfall, and vegetation. Each indicator contributes to a similarity score based on the selected target profile. Users can explore ranked Earth locations, compare their characteristics, and understand why certain locations receive higher or lower similarity scores.

TwinWorld also includes a validation section that distinguishes between documented analog relationships supported by published sources and exploratory hypotheses that have not yet been scientifically confirmed. This helps avoid presenting predictions as established scientific facts.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python, with CSV datasets for organizing and processing geographic information. It combines data analysis, interactive visualization, and a user-friendly interface to make planetary analog research easier to explore.

The main benefit of TwinWorld is that it provides an accessible way to investigate Earth environments that may help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts understand the challenges of exploring the Moon and Mars. It also highlights the limitations of using only a small set of environmental indicators.
